title: Writing Bug Reports for Software Repair Agents: What Information Matters Most?
abstract: arXiv:2607.09553v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Software development is increasingly moving toward agentic-first workflows. This includes AI agents responsible for generating initial fixes for submitted issue reports. In this setting, issue reports are no longer merely documentation for human maintainers; they become the primary task specification for the agent. However, little is known about how such reports should be written to maximize the agent's chances of producing a correct fix. We study what makes a bug report agent-ready. Starting from the SWE-Bench Verified benchmark (i.e. a collection of 500 real repository issues with human-written gold patches and test suites for evaluating generated fixes) we manually classify each issue by change type (e.g. bug fix vs refactoring) and annotate each sentence with its information type, such as observed behavior, expected behavior, reproduction steps, localization cues, and suggested fixes. translated_title: 为软件修复智能体撰写错误报告：哪些信息最重要？
translated_abstract: 软件开发正日益转向以智能体为先的工作流程，其中包括负责为提交的问题报告生成初步修复方案的AI智能体。在这种背景下，问题报告不再仅仅是供人类维护者参考的文档，而是成为智能体的主要任务规范。然而，关于这类报告应如何撰写才能最大化智能体产生正确修复的机会，目前知之甚少。我们研究什么样的错误报告才是“智能体可就绪”的。以SWE-Bench Verified基准（即包含500个真实仓库问题的集合，附带人工编写的黄金补丁和用于评估生成修复的测试套件）为起点，我们手动将每个问题按变更类型分类（例如错误修复与重构），并对每个句子标注其信息类型，如观察到的行为、预期行为、复现步骤、定位线索和建议修复方案。我们聚焦于代表错误修复的441个问题……
tldr: 该论文通过对SWE-Bench Verified基准中的真实问题报告按变更类型分类并逐句标注信息类型（如观察行为、复现步骤、定位线索等），系统研究如何撰写“智能体可就绪”的错误报告，以最大化AI修复智能体生成正确修复的机会。
en_tdlr: This paper studies what makes a bug report "agent-ready" by manually classifying issue types and annotating per-sentence information types in the SWE-Bench Verified benchmark, aiming to maximize the chances of AI software repair agents producing correct fixes.
